claim: Fexagratinib x AKT1/2/3 (MyCancerGenomeClinicalTrial): caused by the AZD5363 alias on iuphar.ligand:7707
class: database-grounded error hypothesis, NOT verified as to mechanism; best class for the pair itself: absence of a measurement (trial-level listing, no assay)
evidence: DGIdb live GraphQL 2026-11-04: concept iuphar.ligand:7707 has aliases AZD-4547, AZD5363, AZD4547, CHEMBL3348846, so the alias exists (while GtoPdb ligand 7709 = capivasertib = AZD5363). But interactionClaims for AKT1/2/3 on that concept show drugClaim name AZD4547 (source MyCancerGenomeClinicalTrial), not AZD5363, so the rows are the AZD4547 claim, not a capivasertib claim merged by alias. In the cache the same rows sit on ncit:C88272. The same MCG-trial source lists AKT1/2/3 for everolimus, omipalisib (GSK2126458), ipatasertib, MK2206, perifosine: a pathway or trial gene list, not a target assay. Public registrations pair AZD4547 and AZD5363 as separate arms of one multi-arm trial (NCT02664935, NCT02117167, NCT02299999, NCT02465060). GtoPdb 7707 interactions: FGFR1-4, IGF1R, KDR only. ChEMBL CHEMBL3348846: 206 activities, FGFR1-4, KDR, no AKT.
limit: MCG trial row not public; the mapping from trial listing to claim is inference. The alias is a real DGIdb defect but is not shown to produce these rows. Exclusion from signed propagation remains defensible, with the reason restated: unmeasured listing, not capivasertib identity transfer.
